title: Contingency Funding Planning

maps.tested: Rated Very Important with no crash-course substitute. No exam recall names it, which makes it an under-covered risk rather than a safe skip.
maps.specifics: Governance of the CFP, trigger design and escalation, the menu of contingent funding sources and their reliability under stress, and testing requirements. Treat as thin-evidence-but-high-rating.

vardeezReading: LTR-11: Very Important, with the note that the entire chapter is important and the crash course notes should be referred to.

selectors.name: Governance of the CFP: roles
selectors.what: Who designs, invokes, oversees and approves the contingency funding plan: the treasurer (with the CFO) may invoke it and convene the liquidity crisis team, the LCT designs it and submits it to senior management for approval, the management committee oversees the LCT and consults the board. Also who owns which communication relationship (treasury with regulators, rating agencies and clearing banks; investor relations with investors, analysts and media).

selectors.name: Trigger design and escalation levels
selectors.what: Early warning indicators (market, industry and institution-specific, chosen to tell idiosyncratic from systemic stress), liquidity health measures and their limits, and escalation levels (three to five is common) where movement up or down is explicitly considered and approved by the LCT, not automatic.

selectors.name: Contingent actions and their reliability
selectors.what: The menu of contingent liquidity actions, how available each is under systemic versus idiosyncratic stress, the impediments and mitigants, and signalling risk: early defensive steps or use of an emergency facility may signal weakness and reduce later availability, so drastic actions belong to later stages.

selectors.name: Testing requirements and operational readiness
selectors.what: Which elements of the CFP are tested periodically: debt issuance, brokered deposits and limited securities sales may be tested, whereas divestitures, large asset sales and central bank borrowing may be impractical or unavailable for testing; also governance, escalation, communication and reporting, with simulation exercises improving response times and exposing gaps.

notSelected: LTR-11 a (the relationship between the CFP and liquidity stress testing, BAU versus high-impact low-probability events) and the rest of LTR-11 b (supervisory backdrop, five design considerations, portfolio of CFPs by entity, integration of liquidity and capital) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer; within LTR-11 c, the scenarios and liquidity gap analysis and the data and reporting components, and the policies and procedures outline, are likewise not covered by any selector.
